definition: Social penetration theory is a social psychology framework used to explain how self-disclosure can create closer interpersonal connection. In this packet, it is applied to the idea that when a person shares more about themselves, others may feel less psychological distance and greater similarity, which is linked to stronger responses toward that person.

reasons: The definition’s framing (“used to explain how self-disclosure can create closer interpersonal connection”) is not directly stated in the packet excerpt; the packet instead specifies live streamers’ self-disclosure effects via psychological distance and perceived homophily in relation to consumers’ purchase intention.

The definition’s “stronger responses toward that person” is too general; the packet ties outcomes specifically to consumers’ purchase intention (and identification/defensiveness), not to a broadly defined set of “stronger responses.”

The definition does not capture the packet’s application context (live streaming commerce and consumer purchase intention), while the packet presents Social Penetration Theory in that specific relationship.
